clue.text: Live in back bedroom in Spanish resort

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: back tells us to read the little word in from right to left

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a shared bedroom

explanation.surface: Someone lives in the back bedroom of a holiday flat on the Spanish coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Benidorm is a well-known package-holiday town on Spain's Costa Blanca.

clue.text: Good sport, tall and ungainly

parts.note: angling, fishing with rod and line, is a sport

explanation.surface: A good sport who happens to be tall and awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes a lanky, loose-limbed, awkward build.

clue.text: 12's tune I'm playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer announces that they are playing one of the composer's tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: '12's' refers to the answer at 12 across, MOZART, so the definition means 'a piece by Mozart'; 'tune' looks like part of the definition but is anagram fodder with I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart wrote many minuets, a stately dance form in triple time, so one is aptly a piece of his.

clue.text: Greenery against variety of red flower

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: a variety of the word red is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is a river, something that flows; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Lush greenery is contrasted with a red-flowered variety of plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdure is lush green vegetation, a literary synonym for greenery.

clue.text: OK for surgery to have musical works originally broadcast by the 22 across

parts.note: operas are musical works for the stage

indicators.note: originally means we take only the opening letter of broadcast

parts.note: 22 across is the word for the nationality of France, and 'the' in that language is le

explanation.surface: A hospital wonders whether broadcasting operas by a foreign company makes a patient fit for surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: An operable condition or patient is one that can be treated surgically.

clue.text: 12's soldier caught virus when embraced by friend

indicators.note: being embraced by a friend means sitting inside the word for friend

parts.note: mate is British slang for friend
a GI is an American soldier
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
flu, influenza, is a virus

explanation.surface: One of the composer's soldiers picked up a bug while being hugged by a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: '12's' points to the answer at 12 across, MOZART: the definition means 'a work by Mozart'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Flute is Mozart's last completed opera, so it is a work of his.

clue.text: Make wrong entry? Horn player has within movement of 12's 5th

indicators.note: the named letter is shifted to a new place within the word for horn player

parts.note: a bugler plays the bugle, a kind of horn
the fifth letter of the composer's name at 12 across is R

explanation.surface: A horn player makes a wrong entry in a movement of the composer's fifth symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a part of a symphony, but here it means moving the R within BUGLER to make BURGLE. 'Wrong entry' is breaking in, not a musician's mistimed entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgle is to break into a building unlawfully, a wrongful entry, hence the question mark.

clue.text: No all-round musical knowledge

indicators.note: all-round says the whole following string is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical
gen is British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone lacks broad knowledge of musicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' looks like an opening reply, but it is the whole definition; the bare noun for a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative is a refusal or denial, the same as saying no.

clue.text: 12's 38th affliction, changing hands

indicators.note: changing hands swaps left for right, L for R, inside the word for affliction

parts.note: a plague is a widespread affliction

explanation.surface: The composer's thirty-eighth symphony seems a blight when the hands switch over.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the usual abbreviations for left and right, the two hands. Mozart's Symphony No 38 is nicknamed the Prague.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 38 is known by the nickname of the Czech capital where it premiered.

clue.text: See 2
Emphasises if good for English servants

indicators.note: good for English means G stands in place of E in the word

parts.note: underlines means stresses or emphasises

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that being good is the right quality for English servants.
explanation.walkthrough: The last E of UNDERLINES is the one replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlings are subordinates who serve others, so servants fits.

clue.text: 24 across 2 15 broadcasting works of beauty found around castle?

indicators.note: broadcasting signals that the phrase is to be heard said over the air

parts.words: works of beauty found around castle
parts.note: works of beauty are art; what is found around a castle is its moat, so the art is the moat's art

explanation.surface: A radio station broadcasts beautiful artworks discovered near a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answers at 24 across, 2 and 15 run together, the composer's full given names.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus is the given name of the composer Mozart, so his full name fits.

clue.text: Broken chord with a name in mythical Greek

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A musician plays a broken chord named after a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'broken chord' is a real musical term (an arpeggio), which hides 'Broken' as the anagram signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromache, wife of Hector of Troy, is a figure from Greek legend.

clue.text: Checked expert's entry to clarinet part

indicators.note: entry to means one word goes into the middle of another

parts.note: a reed is the vibrating mouthpiece part of a clarinet
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: An expert checks the entry of the clarinet in a passage of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuffed means repelled or held back, which is a sense of checked.

clue.text: Film produced in Australia

indicators.note: in places the word for produced inside the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: A film made in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus is the 1984 Oscar-winning film about the composer at 12 across.

clue.text: In the manner of Rabelais' first letter in Paris, you enunciated vulgarly, without gravity

definitions.text: In the manner of Rabelais' first letter in Paris

indicators.note: enunciated means the word you is pronounced, giving a single letter that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

indicators.note: without tells us to take a letter out of the word vulgarly

parts.note: g is the symbol for gravity, the acceleration due to it

explanation.surface: A French writer spoke vulgarly, without any seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabelais' first letter is R, and in Paris the R is pronounced at the back of the throat with the uvula.
explanation.definitionFit: The French R is a uvular sound, so saying it like a Parisian is articulating with the uvula.

clue.text: 12's unfinished piece, we hear, covered by rock band

indicators.note: covered by means the inner piece is wrapped inside the band's name

parts.note: REM is the American rock band

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: piece sounds the same as peace, which is quiet

explanation.surface: The composer's famously unfinished piece is covered by a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns piece into its sound-alike peace, i.e. QUIET, cut to QUIE by 'unfinished'. Mozart's Requiem was left unfinished at his death, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Requiem in D minor is one of his works, completed by others after he died.

clue.text: Run away holding some scanties, somewhat revealingly cut?

indicators.note: holding means the word for run away contains the other piece

parts.note: to elope is to run away to marry

indicators.note: some signals that only part of the word scanties is used, its opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone runs off clutching skimpy underwear, a rather revealing cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealingly cut' suggests skimpy clothing, but an escalope is a thin slice of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin, beaten slice of meat, a scanty cut, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: 12's 41st, by Jove!

definitions.meaning: the composer's Symphony No 41 carries the nickname of the chief Roman god
Jove is another name for the chief Roman god, king of the gods

explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link, and the exclamation 'by Jove!' gives the surface its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 41 is nicknamed after the Roman sky god, also called Jove.

clue.text: House number for singer in capital

parts.note: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer

explanation.surface: A house number is assigned to a singer living in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city of the US state of Hawaii.

clue.text: Honour given to boy king …

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An honour is awarded to a young king.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Dawn chorus intro? Female wren heard first

indicators.note: first says that piece comes ahead of the chorus intro
heard means the clue words are pronounced, giving letters that sound like them

parts.note: F for female followed by wren, whose W is silent when spoken
the introduction or opening of the word chorus is its first two letters, CH

explanation.surface: The dawn chorus starts with a female wren singing first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn chorus' is a phrase, but 'Dawn' alone is the definition, the comedian Dawn French.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn French is a British comedy actress, so her first name leads to her surname.

clue.text: … or a gift endlessly rejected by 12's groom

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run of letters is read in reverse
endlessly means the run of letters stops short of the end of the final word, so the last letter of gift is dropped

explanation.surface: A gift is spurned by the composer's bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves OR A GIF, which 'rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the groom in Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro.

clue.text: Confess about end of marriage, moving apart thus

definitions.text: Confess about end of marriage, moving apart thus

indicators.note: about means the word for confess goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to sing is slang for to confess, to inform

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of marriage is used
moving means the letters of apart are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone owns up about a marriage ending, splitting up as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' makes the whole clue the definition too: owning up that a marriage is over is what a couple moving apart does.
explanation.definitionFit: Separating is the act of moving apart, such as a couple splitting at the end of a marriage.

clue.text: See 24 down
Transformer in which we reversed current

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the word for current backwards

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is anything that flows, like a current or river

explanation.surface: An electrical transformer reverses the current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformer' suggests electricity, but it is a person who changes shape at full moon; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf transforms from human into wolf, so it is a shape-changer.

clue.text: 12's K replacing L? O heck!

indicators.note: replacing reads as re-placing, putting the letters back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a K for an L and exclaims in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's works are numbered with K numbers from Ludwig von Köchel's catalogue, the K of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Köchel compiled the catalogue of Mozart's works whose numbers are prefixed with K.

clue.text: Doctor's composed operas without aural aid

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
composed means put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor writes operas without needing a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eardrops are medicinal drops put in the ear, an aid to the ear.
